summary: Castle Rock lookout, Willamette NF near McKenzie Bridge: cabins 1914-1938, burned by vandals in 1974; only anchor bolts and a solar panel and antenna remain.

facts.design: L-4 cab (final, 1938); earlier D-6 cupola cabin (1924)
facts.status_note: Burned by vandals on 31 October 1974. The summit now holds a solar panel and an antenna; only anchor bolts are reported from the old tower.

access.note: Forest Service trailhead listed as open. Reached by a rough gravel road (Road 480) and a short trail.

visit.trail_note: About 1.2 to 1.25 miles on foot from the trailhead to the summit, per Eugene Weekly and Oregon Hikers. No lookout remains to climb.

events.note: Tent camp set up on the site, per the Forest Fire Lookout Association. Other sources start with a shelter in 1917 or 1918.
A forest guard was stationed on Castle Rock in August 1915, per a newspaper report.
Shelter, per firelookout.com. Eugene Weekly gives 1918 for the same shelter.
Shelter built, per Eugene Weekly. Firelookout.com gives 1917 for the same shelter.
Laurell Canning, a University of Oregon student, stationed at the lookout. She reported the Avenue Creek fire.
Hexagonal log cabin, per the Forest Fire Lookout Association and firelookout.com. Dates for the later houses differ by source.
Mrs. J. D. Baughman, lookout on Castle Rock, reported a large fire on Mount Hagan near Blue River.
Newspapers report a new lookout house finished in August 1923, built with glass on all four sides. It is not clear if this replaced the 1921 cabin.
D-6 cupola cabin, per the Forest Fire Lookout Association and firelookout.com. Eugene Weekly describes a cupola cabin in 1924. A weebly transcription dates a D-6 house to c.1925.
Claude Robinson, University of Oregon graduate, served as lookout.

L-4 cab replaced the 1924 cabin, per the Forest Fire Lookout Association and firelookout.com. A 1938 newspaper report says construction had started on a new station. Eugene Weekly calls it a bigger lookout cabin.
Grace M. Harbick to handle the lookout alone, per a newspaper report.
Doug Newman staffed the lookout each summer in the 1960s, per Eugene Weekly. The year given is the start of that decade.
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register on April 24, 2011.

corrections.why: The lookout that stood until it burned in 1974 was the L-4 cab built in 1938. The D-6 cupola cabin of 1924 was the one it replaced.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Fire Lookout Association gives a tent camp in 1914. firelookout.com gives a shelter in 1917, and Eugene Weekly gives a shelter built in 1918. A 1915 newspaper report shows a guard stationed there. The story gives all of these and does not choose one.

The Forest Fire Lookout Association and firelookout.com date a hexagonal cabin to 1921 and the D-6 cupola cabin to 1924. Newspapers describe a new house finished in August 1923, and the weebly transcription dates a D-6 house to c.1925. The story reports these as differing dates.

firelookout.com gives about four miles southwest of McKenzie Bridge. Newspaper reports from February and April 1923 give six and five miles. The story gives the four-mile figure and reports the newspaper figures.

notes_for_editor: Dates for the first shelter and the 1920s houses disagree across sources; the story reports the disagreement. The 1974 burn date appears in three sources; no primary newspaper of 1974 was read. Eugene Weekly (Nov 2024) is the latest source for the site today, so the current condition is as of 2024. Eugene Weekly describes anchor bolts from an old tower, while the record says kind: ground; check the kind field. The newspaper quotes come from a weebly transcription, not the original papers. The 1938 report is a newspaper lead, so the story does not claim a completion date for the L-4.
